newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. Africa says Zaire's Mobutu, rebel chief to meet.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa says Zaire's Mobutu, rebel chief to meet.

text.p: Face-to-face talks between Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila will take place "shortly", South Africa said on Tuesday.
"The talks will take place shortly...it will be a meeting between President Mobutu and Laurent Kabila," Pieter Swanepoel, spokesman for the Foreign Affairs Department, told Reuters.

Swanepoel said the talks would be presided over by President Nelson Mandela and followed extensive consultation with both the rebels and Mobutu's government. South Africa's Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will also take part.
In a statement issued later, the Foreign Affairs Department said a venue had been agreed upon by both sides and final discussions on a date were being concluded.
"The venue will be announced in due course," Swanepoel said.
The statement said the talks had been arranged in close cooperation with United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun.
Earlier a South African newspaper said the talks could be held on one of the country's warships in international waters.
Business Day said Mobutu could meet Kabila on the naval supply ship Outeniqua.
Meeting on a ship, possibly off the coast of Zaire or off the neighbouring Angolan enclave of Cabinda, would allow the cancer-stricken Mobutu to hold talks close to Zaire, the paper said.
